title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 249
paragraphs: Now the Ister, since it flows through inhabited land, is known by the reports of many. But of the sources of the Nile no one can give an account, for the part of Libya through which it flows is uninhabited and desert. About its course, however, as much as it was possible to learn by the most diligent inquiry has been told; and it flows out into Egypt. Now Egypt lies nearly opposite to the mountain districts of Cilicia; and from there to Sinope, which lies on the Euxine Sea, is a journey in the same straight line of five days for a man travelling without baggage; and Sinope lies opposite to the place where the Ister runs out into the sea. Thus I think the Nile passes through the whole of Libya and is of equal length with the Ister.
Of the Nile, then, let this much suffice.
